characters.name: In General
characters.description: Suspiciously Similar Substitute: To the Steam Team from the original series, as they're a team who comprises of the main characters.

characters.name: Thomas the Tank Engine
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: While Thomas maintains his cheekiness and is prone to being stubborn and egotistical, he is generally far more cheerful and friendly compared to his book and show counterpart, where, while mostly pleasant, can be a mischievous and pettyJerkasseven post-Character Development. Adaptational Personality Change:Downplayed. It's shown in "Snowplow Struttin'" that Thomas loves to wear his snowplow even when its not snowing, which comes in stark contrast to the original books and show, where Thomashateshis snowplow and prefers to avoid wearing it when possible. Catchphrase: Thomas does have a good amount of catchphrases, including "Here comes Thomas!" "All engines go!" "Aww, bolts!" "Rusty rail spikes!" and "Chugga-chugga whoo-hoo!" It's All About Me: While he is friendly and does care about the others around him, there are some points where he is stubborn or egotistical, such as in "Rules of the Game", where he was upset when his friends didn't have fun in the obstacle course his way, and in "Dragon Run", where he refused to share his dragon cargo. He ends up realizing his mistakes at the last minute. Keet: Even moreso than the version from later seasons of the original show.

characters.name: Percy the Small Engine
characters.description: Catchphrase: "Percy perfect!" Compressed Vice: In one episode, he suddenly develops a fear of climbing up high hills, despite being able to do so with almost no problems early on in this same continuity. Hedoesretain a fear of heights in other episodes; however, those are for high mountains and areas in mines, where in that episode it was just simple hills in the grassy fields he seemed to have no trouble with before. Primal Fear: Retains his fear of the dark like in the original show. Shrinking Violet: Downplayed; Percy is occasionally nervous about seemingly intimidating topics, but once he gets the memo he returns to being his usual happy and friendly self.

characters.name: Nia the Helpful Engine
characters.description: Adorably Precocious Child: Nia is far and away the most mature of the core five, being able to plan her delivery routes much like Gordon would. Catchphrase: "Let's rock and roll!" Nature Lover: She is very enthusiastic on the natural world. The Navigator: She can plan her own routes, with the only obstacles being unforeseen circumstances. The Perfectionist: Downplayed, but Nia occasionally struggles with unforeseen obstacles to her original plans, with her reluctance to change her current plan or making a new one often being to her detriment.

characters.name: Kana the Speedy Engine
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: She was created specifically for the reboot. Catchphrase: "Electric!" Graceful Ladies Like Purple: Averted. Kana may be a feminine shade of lilac but she is a hardcore tomboy who is more than willing to get messy. OOC Is Serious Business: Despite her extreme enjoyment of going fast, she's the first to tell Nia not to go too fast while pulling the huge fishtank in "Fast Friends". For an addedContinuity Nod,she claims she learned it from when speed wasn't all it took to win the Sodor Cup. Shock and Awe: She's shown to have an aura of electricity around her, which she'll use to make faces and the like.

characters.name: Devious Diesel
characters.description: Adaptational Heroism: Diesel was a scheming trickster in the original; here, he's become one of Thomas' friends with no grudge against steamies. While still retaining some occasional selfish or devious moments, he's treated more as a slightly naughty friend of Thomas rather than the show's recurring villain. Birds of a Feather: His mischievous personality means that he tends to get along with the Troublesome Trucks better than most. Broken Pedestal: He idolizes Farona and Frederico in the "Race for the Sodor Cup" movie, even hoping they'll win over Thomas and Kana. However, when they cheat by lowering the drawbridge, Diesel loses respect for them. Catchphrase: "Sparkin'!" Jerkass Has a Point: While he can certainly contend with Thomas in terms of selfish or over-competitive moments, he will sometimes call out when Thomas acts just as out-of-line. In "Dragon Run" for example, the others clearly agree with Diesel that Thomas is being possessive of his cargo afterthey helped him out, though they also add it's still not Diesel's or their's to take forcibly.

characters.name: Carly the Crane
characters.description: A yellow crane engine who works on Sodor performing maintenance duties. Adaptation Species Change: Well, vehicle change to be more accurate in her case. In the original show, Carly was a stationary crane who worked at Brendam Docks alongside Cranky. In this show, however, she is a diesel engine with a large crane attached to her roof. Ascended Extra: Went from a minor character in the original series to a member of the main cast in the reboot. Catchphrase: "Crankin'!" Wrench Wench: She and Sandy do the railway's repair work.

characters.name: Sandy the Rail Speeder
characters.description: A pink railway speeder who works with Carly. The Baby of the Bunch: She's the smallest of the main characters and acts like a younger child compared to the other child engines. Canon Foreigner: She was created specifically for the reboot. Every Device Is a Swiss-Army Knife: The amount of tools she can deploy isabsolutely ridiculous. Gadgeteer Genius: Sandy is always tinkering, and always comes up with a new invention.

characters.name: Bruno the Brake Car
characters.description: Anautisticred caboose who helps the engines with heavy deliveries. Badass Bookworm: He is knowledgeable, but also has brakes strong enough to stop a heavy train from behind. Canon Foreigner: He was created specifically for the reboot. He then became aCanon Immigrantwhen it was confirmed that he would appear in the 2026 CGI reboot. Clock King: He memorizes everyone's schedule each day, so he knows where and when every engine should be working. Creepy Monotone: Subverted. Bruno speaks in monotone with little emotional fluctuation, but the other engines seem to understand why and don't find him off-putting at all.

characters.name: Gordon the Big Engine
characters.description: Adaptational Job Change:He now assigns the young engines their jobs for the day, something only Sir Topham Hatt originally ever did.He also has yet to be seen pulling his express coaches, and is much more content with goods deliveries than he was before. He now assigns the young engines their jobs for the day, something only Sir Topham Hatt originally ever did. He also has yet to be seen pulling his express coaches, and is much more content with goods deliveries than he was before. Adaptational Nice Guy: Originally a pompous and prideful engine in the original show, the reboot alters him into aReasonable Authority Figurewhom the engines often turn to. And as mentioned before, he is now quite happy to regularly pull goods trains, which were hisBerserk Buttonin the original series. Catchphrase: "Well, this is a fine how do you do..." usually spoken after something terrible happens to him.

characters.name: James the Red Engine
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: The earlier James was generally a vain and egotisticalJerk with a Heart of Gold, but he's a lot nicer here. He still has a bit of aSmall Name, Big Egothing going on, but he's pretty jovial and friendly about it. Large Ham: Outside of his pleasant behavior, James can be very loud and melodramatic. Nice Guy: James is friendlier here than in the original show, as he is seen greeting the other engines (mostly Thomas and Percy), he doesn't show off that much, and he rarely loses his cool. Small Name, Big Ego: Toned down compared to earlier incarnations, but it's still there. He's quick to brag about himself, calling himself "handsome and incredibly charming." Why Did It Have to Be Snakes?: He is afraid of dragons, as revealed in "Dragon Run."

characters.name: Annie & Clarabel
characters.description: Dub Name Change: Like the original show, Clarabel's name was changed to Clarabella for the Latin American Spanish dub. Identical Twin ID Tag: In the original, their nameplates were how to tell them apart; they've lost them here, and the way to tell them apart is by their eye color (brown for Annie, grey for Clarabel) and the freckles on Clarabel's cheeks. Clarabel's crests also havefourwings, whereas Annie's only has two.

characters.name: Emily the Stirling Engine
characters.description: Demoted to Extra: In the original series, she was one of the main characters. Here, she becomes a side character. Red Oni, Blue Oni: The blue to Sir Topham Hatt's red; Unlike Sir Topham, Emily always maintains her composure in a slight delay, whereas he tends toFreak Out.

characters.name: Whiff the Garbage Engine
characters.description: The Ghost: While he was mentioned and planned to appear in the first season, Whiff ultimately never appeared on screen until well into the second season. Mad Scientist: Is always tinkering with something behind the scenes. Nerd Glasses: It wouldn't be Whiff without them.

characters.name: Cranky the Crane
characters.description: The Grump: He's rarely seen smiling. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He still cares about others even if he rarely shows it.

characters.name: Edward the Blue Engine
characters.description: Adapted Out: Subverted. Originally Edward was not planned to be in the show, but was added back last minute when the animators needed more engines to work with. Demoted to Extra: In the original series, he was one of the main characters before being written off. Here, he goes down to a mere background character with silent cameos every time he appears. The Voiceless: Unlike the original series, Edward does not speak whatsoever. Rick Suvalle hasstatedthat the show staff always hoped Edward and Henry would be able to speak, and included them in episode plans, but the production crew would always give Edward and Henry's lines to another character who had already been cast, mainly due to the expense of hiring new voice actors. You Don't Look Like You: He has a 6-6-0 wheel arrangement this time around, as opposed to being a 4-4-0 like both his Railway Series and original TV series counterparts. He also appears to be almost as big as Gordon and Henry. Original Edward is far from the smallest engine, but James, Henry, and Gordon are bigger than him.

characters.name: Henry the Green Engine
characters.description: Demoted to Extra: In the original series, he was one of the main characters before being written off, and is one of the three earliest characters introduced in the books. Here, like Edward and Duck, he goes down to a mere background character with no speaking roles. The Voiceless: Unlike the original series, Henry does not speak whatsoever. Rick Suvalle hasstatedthat the show staff always hoped Henry and Edward would be able to speak, and included them in episode plans, but the production crew would always give Edward and Henry's lines to another character who had already been cast, mainly due to the expense of hiring new voice actors. You Don't Look Like You: One of his domes is yellow now (due to sharing Percy's colour palette) and he’s a 2-6-2 instead of his original 4-6-0 wheel arrangement (due to his model being modified from Gordon).

characters.name: Toby the Tram Engine
characters.description: Cool Old Guy: Very amicable, and still relatively spry despite his age. Demoted to Extra: In the original series, he was one of the main characters before being written off, though even after being brought down to a supporting role he still had a few roles as a primary character. Here, he only appearsoncein the second season before making a couple of minor appearances in the third and fourth seasons. The first season is notably the only season of the entire franchise, let alone the series, from which he is completely absent Miniature Senior Citizens: Toby is established as an elderly adult character, but his scale more accurately matches the child characters. Truer to the Text: While still having some elements of the insecurity present in later eras of the original show, this version of Toby is closer to his original depiction as a contentCool Old Guy. Backstory-wise, the show even confirms in his debut that he comes from East Anglia, where his old line was located in the books, as opposed to the original series placing his line on a northern part of Sodor separate from the other engines.

characters.name: Kenji
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Kenji has made far more appearances in the reboot than in the original series; justified in that he was only introduced in the final season of the original show. Super-Speed: He is most famous for his speed.

characters.name: Hiro
characters.description: Demoted to Extra: Hiro only appears in a single special before only appearing through portrait cameos or silent appearances in web videos, whereas before he was a recurring secondary character in the pre-BWBA CGI episodes. Old Master: He is an elderly tender engine with years of wisdom.

characters.name: Harold the Helicopter
characters.description: Token Flyer: He is the sole aircraft in the series known to be sentient. You Don't Look Like You: Harold's face is not part of his bodywork, which is a huge departure from his original series counterpart.

characters.name: Bulstrode the Barge
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: He is friendly and helpful, unlike his original series counterpart who is aJerkass. Ascended Extra: He appeared only once in the original series, but has made semi-frequent appearances inAll Engines Goas the resident boat character.

characters.name: Skiff the Sailboat
characters.description: You Don't Look Like You: As revealed in the short "Skiff Upon the Sea", he now lacks his rail chassis.

characters.name: Yong Bao
characters.description: Demoted to Extra: Aside from the episodes covering his departure and arrival, Yong Bao seldom has a major role, and his appearances in the second season are primarily through cameos. Humble Hero: Yong Bao is renowned for his acts of bravery, but he openly admits that he does get scared and is generally amicable. Nice Guy: Famous as he is, Yong Bao is overwhelmingly an engine who would rather be useful and spend as much time as he is able to with his friends. In fact, he isneverseen acting selfish or rude throughout all of his appearances in the series. Not So Above It All: He joins Thomas in rolling backwards down Cannonball Curve out of fright after the fireworks go off. Red Is Heroic: Bright Chinese red with yellow lining and famous for his acts of bravery.

characters.name: Ashima
characters.description: A brightly-painted hot pink tank engine from India who often visits the Island of Sodor. AcCENT upon the Wrong SylLABle: Zigzagged. Her name is now pronouncedAH-sha-macontrary to the original series’uh-SHEE-ma, though the former is actually the correct pronunciation of the name. Nice Girl: It'srareto see her feel anything but happy. Granted, she doesnotappreciate being looked down upon due to her paintwork. Pink Is Feminine: Much more feminine than Sandy, but Ashima still does her best to pull her weight, and like Sandy doesn't even mind getting dirty in the process. Silk Hiding Steel: Don't let her paintwork fool you, Ashima is a mountain engine and does not like being underestimated because of that paint.

characters.name: The Troublesome Trucks
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: While still ill-behaved, their more malicious traits have been toned down significantly compared the books and original show. Adapted Out: In the original series, the trucks were by far the most common sight on the railway; in the reboot, their numbers have been reduced to just two, with all other rolling stock (besides Annie, Clarabel, Bruno, and two tankers in the second season) being non-sentient. Those Two Guys: While there are a few episodes where only one of the trucks is seen at a time, the vast majority of their appearances rarely show one of them without the other.

characters.name: Sir Topham Hatt
characters.description: The controller of the North Western Railway. Adaptational Name Change: Maintains the familiar Bertram Topham Hatt name as in the original show, but here, he is the fourth Sir Topham Hatt, who in the original book canon was named Richard Topham Hatt. Did Not Think This Through: A lot of his attraction ideas, while they seem exciting in his head, are very much boring in reality. Large Ham: Almost always seenChewing the Scenery. Legacy Character: He's the fourth Sir Topham Hatt in his family.

characters.name: FarmerMcColl
characters.description: The Voiceless: Unlike the original series,Farmer McCollhere is silent.

characters.name: Terence the Tractor
characters.description: Catchphrase: "Yippee!" Cheerful Child: Terence has a fun-loving and cheerful personality and treats work more like a game.

characters.name: Winston
characters.description: Adaptational Personality Change: Is depicted as much more confident in this series compared to his previous characterization as a more demure and uncertain chap. Catchphrase: "Early days!" Know-Nothing Know-It-All: Winston started out clueless but acting confident in his knowledge, but he typically never gotanywhereuntil Thomas helped him out. It took him a while to ask for help, but he quickly became used to it afterward.

characters.name: Salty the Dockside Diesel
characters.description: Cool Old Guy: Very much gives off the vibe of an old sea dog. Talk Like a Pirate: A downplayed version, but it still wouldn't be Salty if hedidn'tengage in this. What Could Have Been: At one point during the design process, Salty was initially going to have yellow wheels, which carried over to the prototype of his motorized toy and early promo art before the team changed them to the original black wheels from the original series.

characters.name: Beresford
characters.description: Big Fun: Very friendly despite his large size. The Big Guy: Of all the characters in the reboot that can move, Beresford is by far the largest of the cast.

characters.name: Darcy the Driller
characters.description: Alliterative Name:Darcy theDriller. Cool Shades: She had a pair of Cool Goggles which actually serve a practical purpose- they come down to protect her eyes when she drills. Drill Tank: She’s a roadheader, meaning she's based on a real-life one of these. Early-Bird Cameo: Briefly appears in Season 2’s “Off The Rails”, but doesn’t actually debut until “What’s The Buzz?”, the first episode of Season 3.

characters.name: Duck the Great Western Engine
characters.description: The Voiceless: Duck never speaks every time he's on screen in Sodor Sings Together. What Could Have Been: During the design process, Duck—much like Salty—was originally planned with yellow wheels and lighter green paint, a direction that initially carried over to his released push-along toy and box art. However, when he made his debut in All Engines Go, he appeared with darker green paint and black wheels instead.

characters.name: Farona and Frederico
characters.description: Two antagonistic yellow and black Spanish electric engines who compete in the Sodor Cup race. Adaptational Nice Guy: In theLet's Raceshorts, Farona and Frederico are written to be good guys instead of the closest thing to villains. Gang of Bullies: Throughout their appearance in ''Race for the Sodor Cup", Farona and Frederico end up bullying Thomas and Kana and predicting that they'll derail. Surprisingly, they haven't done the same to Diesel, their former biggest fan. Hair-Trigger Temper: In the "Bell Race" short, Frederico ended up getting jealous due to Farona competing against him, so he ends up playing rough during the tug-of-war game.He ends up regretting it and accepts losing due to his behavior. Identical Twin ID Tag: Both of them have yellow wheels, but most of Frederico's colors (save for their shared orange stripes) are inverted from Farona's.

characters.name: Jiff and Riff
characters.description: Two other Sodor Cup competitors, but with red liveries. Ascended Extra: The two of them end up making plot-important appearances in the second season after their debut in the first feature-length special. This may be to equalize the new characters' screentime, as Farona and Frederico have the lion's share of it in the film. Genki Girl: It'srareto see either of them upset in any fashion. Graceful Loser: Whereas Farona and Frederico despair at being taken out of the race, Riff and Jiff do nothing but cheer on Thomas and Kana once they get ahead of them. Identical Twin ID Tag: What are yellow and pink on Riff are teal on Jiff.

characters.name: Tess the Troublesome Crane
characters.description: A large teal gantry crane that works at Kellsthorpe. Green and Mean: Tess' main color is teal green, but she's actually much more caring than her snappy demeanor suggests. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Tess can be impatient, rude, and dismissive when her workload is increased, but even if she says something negative, she rarely means it and genuinely cares for others. You Look Familiar: She is basically Carly's original series design with a new face and a green paint job. Younger Than They Look: Tess towers over most of the other characters and she doesn't look that youthful at first glance; you can only tell she's a child character because of her voice.

characters.name: Reginald
characters.description: A mute baker who works at the Peel Godred bakery.
